title: Markets Sink on End of Five-Day Oil Price Decline, Big PMI Beats: Sept. 23, 2026
summary: An end to the five-day streak of sinking oil prices combined with Flash PMIs depicting the strongest month of economic growth in over five years is sending yields to the nosebleeds and hurting risk sentiments on Wall Street. Fuel charges are rising for the first session in six as investors wonder whether there's a realistic path for peace between the US and Iran, with traders balancing President Trump's hardline rhetoric during his UN speech against his more conciliatory tone following talks with Tehran, which he described as very good. The confusion paired with Iranian leadership remaining committed to its firm positions is triggering a turnaround for crude prices and generating much heavier interest rates. Meanwhile, big beats across services and manufacturing in the economic calendar that signaled fast hiring and raging inflation point to an excellent environment for corporate earnings amidst harsh headwinds for Treasuries, as fixed-income observers dial up Fed hike probabilities, GDP projections and cost pressure expectations. The curve's climb is increasingly pronounced at the monetary policy sensitive short end as the complex shifts in bear-flattening fashion. Tighter financial conditions alongside an appreciating greenback are derailing animal spirits, with equities, cryptocurrencies and non-energy commodities suffering losses. Indeed, the four major domestic stock benchmarks are declining with 9 of the 11 principal sectors dropping. Volatility protection instruments are catching bids as a result, as folks brace for more potential downside. Separately, prediction markets are experiencing engagement.
